# Return to a previously focused pane
<!-- generated by docs:update_by_ai -->
<!-- page type: how-to -->

Return keyboard input to a previously focused pane. A pane is one terminal inside a tab; the pane with keyboard focus receives what you type. Start with two different, still-open panes.

## Prepare the pane focus history
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/stores/pane_focus_history.ts -->

1. Click the first pane and keep keyboard focus on that pane for at least half a second.
2. Click the second pane, keep both panes open, and keep keyboard focus on the second pane for at least half a second.

Check that the Back button is enabled. The Back button and Forward button are in the top bar, immediately left of the search button; their arrows point left and right.

## Return to an earlier pane
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->

1. Click the enabled Back button.
2. Check that the first pane receives keyboard input.
3. Click the enabled Forward button to return to the second pane.

Heidrun selects the destination workspace and tab when needed. A pinned pane, kept visible across tabs and workspaces, receives focus where it is without changing the selected workspace or tab.

## Choose a pane from the list
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/components/PaneFocusHistoryButton.vue -->

1. Hold an enabled Back button or Forward button for about half a second until a list opens below the button.
2. Release the button. The list stays open.
3. Click the destination row in the list.

Check that the list closes and the destination pane receives keyboard input. Back lists earlier entries and Forward lists later entries, nearest first. Each row starts with workspace and tab names; distinct coding agent type and custom pane name can follow, with repeated names omitted. Different entries can have identical labels.

## Close the list
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/components/PaneFocusHistoryButton.vue -->

Press Escape to close the list without selecting a history entry. Keyboard focus returns to the button that opened the list. A click outside both the list and that button closes the list and also acts on what you clicked; clicking another pane can give that pane keyboard focus.

## Use the keyboard
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/App.vue -->

The symbol ⌘ means the Command key. Press ⌘[ to go Back or ⌘] to go Forward when the matching direction is available and no window is blocking the shortcut. Check that the destination pane receives keyboard input.

## Troubleshooting
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/components/FilesModal.vue -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/i18n/locales/en/filesModal.json -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/lib/pane_focus_history.ts -->

### The Back button is disabled

Cause: No earlier entry exists before the current history entry.

Solution:

1. Click the first pane and keep keyboard focus on that pane for at least half a second.
2. Click a second, different pane, keep both panes open, and keep keyboard focus on the second pane for at least half a second.

Check: The Back button becomes enabled.

### The Forward button is disabled

Cause: No later entry exists. Recording a new pane after moving Back removes the later entries.

Solution:

1. If Back is also disabled, follow The Back button is disabled first.
2. Click the enabled Back button once.
3. Avoid focusing a different pane before checking Forward.

Check: Forward becomes enabled.

### The shortcut does nothing while the file explorer is open

The file explorer opens with ⌘P and has a file tree, editor and title Files. The close-button tooltip calls this same window the file browser. This window is separate from the large Git window opened through the Files sidebar section.

Cause: The file explorer reserves these shortcuts for its editor.

Solution:

1. Click the X button at the top right, whose tooltip is "Close the file browser (Escape)".
2. If unsaved changes are reported, click Save all and close. If saving fails, resolve the displayed save problem before attempting closure again.
3. Check that the file explorer is closed and the matching Back or Forward button is enabled, then retry the shortcut.

Cancel keeps the file explorer open: return to editing and stop navigation. Discard the changes closes the file explorer but loses unsaved changes. Escape closes the file explorer only when the editor does not have keyboard focus and no menu, name box, selected row, difference view or search text consumes Escape first; otherwise use X.

Check: After the file explorer closes and an enabled direction is used, the destination pane receives keyboard input.

## Related pages

- [Keyboard shortcuts](/documentation/shortcuts): other keyboard actions.
- [Browse and open project files](/documentation/browse_project_files): select an existing workspace.

<!-- generated by docs:update_by_ai -->
<!-- page type: how-to -->

Return keyboard input to a previously focused pane. A pane is one terminal inside a tab; the pane with keyboard focus receives what you type. Start with two different, still-open panes.

## Prepare the pane focus history
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/stores/pane_focus_history.ts -->

1. Click the first pane and keep keyboard focus on that pane for at least half a second.
2. Click the second pane, keep both panes open, and keep keyboard focus on the second pane for at least half a second.

Check that the Back button is enabled. The Back button and Forward button are in the top bar, immediately left of the search button; their arrows point left and right.

## Return to an earlier pane
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->

1. Click the enabled Back button.
2. Check that the first pane receives keyboard input.
3. Click the enabled Forward button to return to the second pane.

Heidrun selects the destination workspace and tab when needed. A pinned pane, kept visible across tabs and workspaces, receives focus where it is without changing the selected workspace or tab.

## Choose a pane from the list
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/components/PaneFocusHistoryButton.vue -->

1. Hold an enabled Back button or Forward button for about half a second until a list opens below the button.
2. Release the button. The list stays open.
3. Click the destination row in the list.

Check that the list closes and the destination pane receives keyboard input. Back lists earlier entries and Forward lists later entries, nearest first. Each row starts with workspace and tab names; distinct coding agent type and custom pane name can follow, with repeated names omitted. Different entries can have identical labels.

## Close the list
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/components/PaneFocusHistoryButton.vue -->

Press Escape to close the list without selecting a history entry. Keyboard focus returns to the button that opened the list. A click outside the list never changes pane focus, even when you click another pane; Heidrun blocks that click.

## Use the keyboard
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/App.vue -->

The symbol ⌘ means the Command key. Press ⌘[ to go Back or ⌘] to go Forward when the matching direction is available and no window is blocking the shortcut. Check that the destination pane receives keyboard input.

## Troubleshooting
<!-- source: docs/agents_rules/user_interface/workspaces_tabs_and_panes/pane_focus_history.md -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/components/FilesModal.vue -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/i18n/locales/en/filesModal.json -->
<!-- source: packages/apps/web_frontend/src/lib/pane_focus_history.ts -->

### The Back button is disabled

Cause: No earlier entry exists before the current history entry.

Solution:

1. Click the first pane and keep keyboard focus on that pane for at least half a second.
2. Click a second, different pane, keep both panes open, and keep keyboard focus on the second pane for at least half a second.

Check: The Back button becomes enabled.

### The Forward button is disabled

Cause: No later entry exists. Recording a new pane after moving Back removes the later entries.

Solution:

1. If Back is also disabled, follow The Back button is disabled first.
2. Click the enabled Back button once.
3. Avoid focusing a different pane before checking Forward.

Check: Forward becomes enabled.

### The shortcut does nothing while the file explorer is open

The file explorer opens with ⌘P and has a file tree, editor and title Files. The close-button tooltip calls this same window the file browser. This window is separate from the large Git window opened through the Files sidebar section.

Cause: The file explorer reserves these shortcuts for its editor.

Solution:

1. Click the X button at the top right, whose tooltip is "Close the file browser (Escape)".
2. If unsaved changes are reported, click Save all and close. If saving fails, resolve the displayed save problem before attempting closure again.
3. Check that the file explorer is closed and the matching Back or Forward button is enabled, then retry the shortcut.

Cancel keeps the file explorer open: return to editing and stop navigation. Discard the changes closes the file explorer but loses unsaved changes. Escape closes the file explorer only when the editor does not have keyboard focus and no menu, name box, selected row, difference view or search text consumes Escape first; otherwise use X.

Check: After the file explorer closes and an enabled direction is used, the destination pane receives keyboard input.
